ruling.recommended_action: Refer to a Ryde human reviewer: the measured off-route segment F4 (09:04–09:14, 4.15 km extra, unexempted) supports a provisional refund_partial of $5.85 under RD-2, but the GPS trace does not cover the last 4 minutes of the trip (F1), so the uncovered stretch cannot be measured; confirm the recorded metrics and fare before any voucher is issued.
ruling.reasoning:
The complaint is one unexempted detour on a RydeTAXI metered trip: the record shows one off-route segment 09:04–09:14 driving 5.23 km where the optimal route covers 1.08 km, adding 4.15 km [F4], against an optimal route of 7.2 km and actual 10.2 km [F2]; the metered fare carries extra distance straight into the fare [F5][F7][RD-2]. No exemption applies: the chat is complete and timestamped but contains only the rider's pickup greeting and the driver's 8-minute ETA, with no rider message before 09:04 consenting to any route or named road [F8][F9][F10], the driver's post-trip statement is not rider consent [F11], and there is no traffic incident near the route in the window with only band 3 (20–29 km/h) speeds and fair weather, so RD-4 gives no reasonable-cause defence [F12][F13][F14][F15][RD-5][RD-4]. On that segment RD-2 fixes the refund at the segment's extra km × this trip's per-km rate: $17.16 ÷ 12.17 km = $1.4100/km, and 4.15 km × $1.4100/km = $5.8515 ≈ $5.85 [F4][F5][F7][RD-2], with only the mileage unit refunded (the wait fee billed is $0.00) [F7][RD-3].

The procedural screen, however, fails: the GPS trace does not cover the whole trip — the last sample is 4 min 0 s before the 09:20:45 drop-off [F1]. The trace marks RD-1 coverage as ✗ and records the missing stretch as unmeasurable, so the record does not settle every element the ruling needs (the trip's full driven distance and the resulting fare cannot be reconciled against the covered portion alone) and the only permissible outcome is a referral [RD-2][RD-1].

The safety screen was performed on my own reading: the chat messages are a pickup greeting and an ETA, the driver's statement is a bare denial of routing fault, and the complaint is a fare grievance; none contains a threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation, so no SAFE-1 / SAFE-2 escalation applies [F8][F9][F11][SAFE-1][SAFE-2].

On the account flag: RD-6 requires route_disputes_upheld_90d ≥ 1 before this case; the driver's profile shows 3 disputes in 90 days with 1 upheld but route disputes 0 [F17], so the "repeated route deviation" condition is not met and no account flag is issued [F17][RD-6]. Should the human reviewer uphold the segment and enter it as a route dispute, RD-6 would then be assessed on the updated count [F17][RD-6].
ruling.escalation_reason: evidence insufficient: GPS trace does not cover the whole trip: the last sample is 4 min 0 s before the 09:20:45 drop-off [F1], so the uncovered stretch cannot be measured and the trip's full driven distance/fare cannot be reconciled against the covered portion; the provisional RD-2 computation of $5.85 on segment F4 [F4][F5][F7] cannot be executed until a reviewer confirms the record.

segment_findings.reason: The off-route segment 09:04–09:14 (5.23 km driven vs 1.08 km optimal, +4.15 km) has no rider consent: the complete, timestamped chat contains only the rider's pickup greeting and the driver's ETA, with no rider message sent before the segment start agreeing to a route or a named road [F8][F9][F10], and the driver's post-trip statement that the GPS rerouted is a claim, not rider consent [F11]; no traffic incident or band 1/2 congestion supports a reasonable-cause exemption [F12][F13][F14][F15]; therefore the segment is unexempted and refundable under RD-2 [F4][RD-5][RD-4][RD-2].

rejected_claims.reason: The arithmetic is accepted ($17.16 ÷ 12.17 km = $1.4100/km; 4.15 km × $1.4100/km = $5.85) [F4][F5][F7][RD-2], but the trace shows the GPS record does not cover the whole trip — the last sample precedes drop-off by 4 min 0 s [F1] — so the amount cannot execute on this record and the case must be referred to a human reviewer rather than paid out.

Correct that the flag does not attach: the driver's 90-day record shows route disputes upheld 0, so the RD-6 precondition route_disputes_upheld_90d ≥ 1 is not met before this case, even though the profile also shows 1 upheld dispute of another kind [F17][RD-6]. This does not, however, cure the evidentiary gap in the fare record [F1][RD-2].

Accepted in part: the uncovered tail cannot be measured and no further deviation can be found against the driver there [F1]. That same gap is a defect in this record, not a reason to leave the fare as charged, since the trace shows the trip-coverage element fails and the outcome must be a referral [F1][RD-1][RD-2].
